name: Hydrogen
blurb: 1H is the nucleus essentially all clinical MRI and MRS is built on: spin 1/2, 99.99 percent abundant, and the highest gyromagnetic ratio of any stable nucleus. Tissue water alone supplies about 80 M of protons.
mrNotes: 1H Larmor frequency is 63.87 MHz at 1.5 T, 127.73 MHz at 3 T and 297.2 MHz at 7 T.

Brain water is roughly 80 M while the largest metabolite pools are 1 to 10 mM, so in vivo 1H MRS needs about 3 orders of magnitude of water suppression (CHESS, VAPOR, or metabolite-cycled subtraction).
2H at 0.0115 percent abundance underpins deuterium metabolic imaging with [6,6'-2H2]glucose; its short T1 near 300 ms permits TR of a few hundred ms, partly offsetting the low gamma.
1H hyperpolarization comes from parahydrogen (PHIP, SABRE) or dissolution DNP, not from optical pumping.

isotopes.notes: The MR workhorse. Receptivity is the reference point for every other nucleus.
Spin 1 with a small quadrupole moment, so lines stay narrow in liquids. Used as the lock nucleus in high resolution NMR and as the readout for deuterium metabolic imaging.
Highest gyromagnetic ratio of any nucleus, but beta active. Used for tritium labelling studies in vitro; never used in vivo.

name: Helium
blurb: Helium matters to MR twice over: liquid 4He is the cryogen that holds superconducting magnets below Tc, and hyperpolarized 3He was the first gas used for human lung ventilation imaging.
mrNotes: 3He has the largest gyromagnetic ratio of any noble gas nucleus, -32.44 MHz/T, about 76 percent of 1H.
Spin exchange optical pumping with Rb vapour reaches 3He polarizations of 30 to 60 percent, roughly 10^5 times thermal equilibrium at 3 T.
3He supply depends on tritium decay stockpiles and is scarce, which is the main reason hyperpolarized gas lung MRI moved to 129Xe.
Liquid 4He boils at 4.22 K; modern MRI cryostats are sealed or zero boil off, but a quench still dumps helium gas and needs a working quench pipe.

Helium is the one cell in the susceptibility column that does not follow the CRC table. Its diamagnetism is calculable essentially exactly, and the first-principles value is -1.89e-6 cm3/mol; CRC prints -2.02, which back-solves to a mean square electron radius about 7 percent too large.

isotopes.shiftRange: -70 to +10 for endohedral and dissolved 3He; free lung gas near 0
isotopes.notes: Hyperpolarized 3He lung imaging. Negative gamma, so the sense of precession is opposite to 1H. Diffusion of 3He in airways gives ADC maps sensitive to emphysema.

name: Lithium
blurb: Lithium is the rare psychiatric drug whose own nucleus can be imaged: 7Li is 92.4 percent abundant with spin 3/2 and about 27 percent of the 1H receptivity, so brain lithium can be mapped in patients at therapeutic doses.
mrNotes: Therapeutic brain lithium is only about 0.2 to 0.8 mM, so 7Li MRSI needs 3 T or higher, large voxels (several cm^3) and acquisitions of 15 to 30 min.
7Li relaxation is quadrupolar but the quadrupole moment is small (-4.01 fm^2); brain 7Li T1 runs to several seconds, which sets the repetition time.
7Li resonates near 16.55 MHz/T, close enough to 13C (10.7 MHz/T) and 23Na (11.3 MHz/T) that one broadband X channel usually serves all three.
Brain to serum lithium ratio measured by 7Li MRS is around 0.5, the quantity that motivates most in vivo studies.

isotopes.notes: The practical lithium nucleus. Narrow lines despite spin 3/2 because the quadrupole moment is small and the hydrated Li+ site is nearly symmetric.
Very small quadrupole moment gives exceptionally narrow lines, but receptivity is about 420 times lower than 7Li, so it is used only for isotope-labelled solution studies.

name: Beryllium
blurb: Beryllium has a single NMR active isotope, 9Be, which is 100 percent abundant and moderately receptive, but beryllium is toxic and plays no biological role, so 9Be NMR stays in coordination and materials chemistry.
mrNotes: 9Be is spin 3/2 with Q = +5.288 fm^2; lines are narrow only in high symmetry sites such as [Be(H2O)4]2+ and BeF4^2-.
Beryllium copper is used for non-sparking and low-permeability tooling, but beryllium is not part of standard MRI hardware and machining dust is a serious inhalation hazard.

isotopes.notes: Negative gamma. Chemical shift range is small, about 30 ppm, so resolving beryllium environments needs good field homogeneity.

name: Boron
blurb: Boron reaches in vivo MR through boron neutron capture therapy: 11B is 80 percent abundant with spin 3/2 and about 13 percent of the 1H receptivity, which makes non-invasive boron dosimetry by MRS plausible.
mrNotes: 11B MRS and MRI of boronophenylalanine and BSH have been used to estimate tumour boron before neutron irradiation; practical detection limits are tens of ppm boron in a large voxel.
10B, not 11B, is the neutron capture nucleus, so converting an 11B measurement to a capture dose requires the known isotopic enrichment of the drug.
Boron is a constituent of Nd2Fe14B permanent magnets and of the MgB2 superconductor used in some cryogen-free magnet designs.
11B linewidth is set by quadrupolar relaxation; asymmetric trigonal boron broadens badly while tetrahedral borate sites stay sharp.

isotopes.notes: The preferred boron nucleus: higher abundance, higher gamma and a smaller quadrupole moment than 10B. Probe background from borosilicate glass and BN inserts is a real problem and needs a background suppression sequence.

Spin 3, and although its quadrupole moment is twice that of 11B the spin factor more than cancels it: at the same site 10B lines are about 1.5 times narrower than 11B in Hz (quadrupolar linewidth factors 14.3 fm4 against 22.0 fm4). In ppm they are about twice as broad, because gamma is three times smaller. Occasionally used to confirm an assignment via the 11B/10B linewidth ratio.

name: Carbon
blurb: 13C is the carbon nucleus of MR: spin 1/2, only 1.07 percent abundant and 1.7e-4 as receptive as 1H. Natural abundance in vivo 13C MRS is slow and SAR limited, which is why dissolution DNP of [1-13C]pyruvate changed the field.
mrNotes: Hyperpolarized [1-13C]pyruvate reaches 20 to 40 percent liquid state polarization, a gain above 10,000, but the signal is non-renewable and decays with an in vivo T1 of 30 to 60 s.
Direct 13C MRS needs broadband 1H decoupling and usually NOE; at 3 T and above the decoupling duty cycle is limited by SAR, not by hardware.
The 13C shift range of about 220 ppm spans roughly 7 kHz at 3 T, so transmit bandwidth and slice or slab selection must be checked against chemical shift displacement.
11C (t1/2 20.4 min) is a mainstream PET label (11C-PiB, 11C-choline, 11C-acetate) but is never detected by NMR.

Graphite, and the least representative number in the column. Graphite is the most anisotropic diamagnet here: about -5.2e-6 cm3/mol with B0 in the basal plane against about -253e-6 along c, a factor of forty, so a randomly oriented powder averages nearer -88e-6. The cell carries the in-plane figure, which is why carbon-fibre and pyrolytic-graphite hardware can perturb B0 far more than this number suggests. Diamond is -5.9e-6.

isotopes.notes: Defines the receptivity unit used for X nuclei. Natural abundance 13C MRS of brain glycogen and glutamate turnover, and the target nucleus for dissolution DNP.
PET nuclide, not an NMR nucleus. Listed because 11C tracers are central to nuclear medicine; the moment is from nuclear physics measurements, not from an NMR table.

name: Nitrogen
blurb: Nitrogen is an awkward MR element: the abundant isotope 14N is spin 1 and quadrupolar, while the spin 1/2 alternative 15N is only 0.364 percent abundant with one of the lowest gyromagnetic ratios in common use.
mrNotes: 15N resonates at only 12.95 MHz at 3 T, so probe and preamplifier noise figure, not sample noise, often dominates sensitivity.
15N T1 in quaternary ammonium, nitrile and azo sites can exceed 100 s, which is exactly why hyperpolarized 15N (SABRE, dDNP, parahydrogen) targets those sites.
Liquid nitrogen at 77 K is the thermal shield coolant and the working fluid for cryogenic RF probes; N2 gas is the standard purge in magnet rooms.
N2 is the quenching gas in Rb spin exchange optical pumping cells for 3He and 129Xe, typically a few hundred torr.

isotopes.notes: Abundant but spin 1 with Q = +2.044 fm^2; quadrupolar relaxation broadens all but the most symmetric sites (NH4+, N(CH3)4+). In vivo 14N MRS is not an established technique.

Spin 1/2 and sharp, but receptivity is only 3.8e-6 relative to 1H at natural abundance, so essentially all use is on 15N-enriched or hyperpolarized material. Negative gamma inverts the NOE, which is why INEPT is preferred over NOE enhancement.
PET nuclide (13N-ammonia for myocardial perfusion). Not an NMR nucleus; the sign shown follows the p1/2 proton systematics of its mirror partner 13C, and many tables list the magnitude only.

name: Oxygen
blurb: Oxygen has exactly one magnetic isotope, 17O, spin 5/2 at 0.038 percent natural abundance. It is the only direct MR route to the cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen, and molecular O2 is paramagnetic, which shortens tissue 1H T1.
mrNotes: Inhaled 17O2 is metabolised to H2 17O, and direct 17O MRSI of that water gives CMRO2 without a radiotracer; the sensitivity penalty makes it a 7 T and above method.
17O T1 and T2 in tissue water are both only a few ms and nearly equal, so very short TR (a few ms) and 3D radial or twisted projection readouts recover much of the lost SNR.
17O also acts indirectly: proton exchange with H2 17O shortens 1H T2, and 17O RF decoupling switches that pathway off, giving a 1H-detected 17O measurement.
Molecular O2 is paramagnetic at +3449e-6 cm3/mol; dissolved O2 shortens 1H T1, which is the mechanism behind oxygen enhanced MRI and PFC-based oximetry.

Alone in this column, oxygen is a Curie paramagnet, so +3449e-6 cm3/mol is a value at about 293 K and not a material constant: it falls to roughly +3260e-6 at body temperature. It is also the gas. Liquid O2 at 90 K is +7699e-6 and solid O2 at 54 K is +10200e-6, both far below what Curie scaling would predict, because O2 molecules in contact couple antiferromagnetically.

isotopes.notes: Negative gamma, spin 5/2, Q = -2.558 fm^2. Quadrupolar relaxation is fast, which is a penalty for linewidth but a gift for repetition rate.
PET nuclide. 15O-water is the reference standard for cerebral blood flow and 15O2 for CMRO2, the same quantities 17O MR targets. Not an NMR nucleus.

name: Fluorine
blurb: 19F is the best MR nucleus after 1H: spin 1/2, 100 percent abundant, 94 percent of the 1H frequency and 83 percent of its receptivity, with essentially no detectable endogenous signal in soft tissue.
mrNotes: Tissue background 19F is negligible; the fluoride in bone and teeth is a solid with T2 far too short for conventional imaging, so a 19F image is a pure tracer map.
19F resonates at 120.15 MHz at 3 T versus 127.73 MHz for 1H, only 6 percent apart, so dual-tuned 1H/19F coils need well designed traps and careful decoupling of the two resonances.
Perfluorocarbon emulsions are used for cell tracking and for oximetry: PFC 19F relaxation rate R1 is close to linear in pO2, giving absolute oxygen tension.

The 19F shift range spans about 400 ppm (roughly 48 kHz at 3 T), so multi-resonance agents such as PFOB need broadband excitation or frequency selective acquisition and chemical shift artefact correction.

isotopes.notes: Second only to 1H for practical MR sensitivity. Used for perfluorocarbon cell labelling and oximetry, and for direct MRS of fluorinated drugs such as 5-fluorouracil and fluoxetine.

The dominant clinical PET nuclide (18F-FDG, 18F-florbetapir, 18F-PSMA). Its ground state is spin 1, but the magnetic and quadrupole moments are not reliably established in the standard compilations, so they are left null here rather than guessed.
